To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

B cell receptor ( BCR ) signaling triggers reactivation of Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpes virus ( KSHV ) from latency in B cells, and that phosphatidylinositide 3-kinases (PI3Ks) and X-box-binding proteins (XBP- 1 ) mediate the BCR -induced activation of KSHV.
the B cell receptor is a stimulus for the reactivation of latent virus in B cells.
BCR signaling triggers KSHV reactivation in latently infected B cells and that this process requires the activation of the PI3K pathway as well as of XBP-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that mediate BCR-triggered KSHV reactivation in B lymphocytes and the role of XBP-1 and PI3K in these processes.
the molecular and cellular events that lead to the reactivation of latent viral genomes in infected B cells.
the molecular mechanisms of KSHV latency and reactivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B cell receptor is a potent stimulus for KSHV reactivation in B cell lymphoma cells and that PI3K and XBP-1 are two important factors in this context.

the reactivation of the latent KSHV genome in latently infected B cells is a complex process, which requires the cooperation of several cellular pathways, such as the BCR signaling cascade, the PI3K/Akt pathway and the unfolded protein response (UPR).
the B cell receptor is the main stimulus for KSHV reactivation in B lymphocytes and that this process is mediated by PI3K and XBP-1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactivation of latent viral DNA is dependent on PI3K and XBP-1, but not on NF-κB or AP-1.
we established a B cell model system for the reactivation of latent viral genomes in B cells and we could identify two important factors for this process.
the reactivation of latent virus by the BCR is mediated by a PI3K-XBP-1 pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BCR is an important stimulus that can lead to reactivation of Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpes virus (KSHV).
the activation of the BCR in latently infected B cells leads to the reactivation of latent viral gene expression and the production of infectious virus.
the BCR can be used as a stimulus to reprogram latently infected B cells to produce infectious KSHV.
